title: No-cavity, destructive-open enclosure with the display module and its SPI/DC/TE/button nets physically unreachable (EVT board + mechanical spec)
threat: CryptoBilis shape exactly: an implant MCU + LTE module parked in the padding behind the screen, soldered to the display SPI bus (pq1: PA4 CS / PA5 SCK / PA7 MOSI, PB0 DC, PB2 TE) or to the button nets (PA0/PA1), installed between factory and first power. Firmware cannot see this (write-only panel, no MISO), so the only deterministic counter is to leave no space and no reachable copper.
proposal: Write and adopt a mechanical/PCB security spec for the MP revision of AL_A66_MB: (1) zero void behind the panel — panel bonded to a rigid backer that fills the cavity, display FPC captured under the EMI can with the connector potted; (2) SPI1/DC/TE/button traces routed on inner layers with no vias to the outer layers in the display region, and NO test pads on SPI1, I2C1, I2C4, PA0/PA1 at MP (EVT currently brings out PB8/PB9 and the 10-pin SWD pads); (3) ultrasonic-welded or otherwise destructive-open shell (Ledger Gen5 / Cypherock model) so any opening is irreversible and visible; (4) verify the ODM's BOOT0-strap-at-MP claim on silicon so the sealed unit's ROM-DFU via the SBU bridge (A8<->VBUS) is physically gone; (5) publish Gerbers, pinned BOM (exact passives), and reference photos / X-ray / weight of a sealed known-good unit so the design is golden-free comparable (Parasitic Circus). Keep the SWD pads reachable ONLY through the deliberately-documented verification route (see IMP-02).
rationale: Ledger's own threat model concedes Genuine Check cannot see an implant around an intact SE; its only remedy was photos and a casing that cannot be opened without damage. pq1 has nothing on this axis yet (no enclosure spec, no BOM, cross-check never done) and its EVT units are reflashable over USB-C with a modified cable. Removing the cavity and the copper access is the one measure that does not depend on detection thresholds or on who calibrated a baseline.

vendor_precedent: Ledger Nano Gen5 casing 'cannot be opened without visible and irreversible damage' (support article 4404382029329); Cypherock ultrasonic-welded shell + Keylabs audit flagging exposed test points as a supply-chain jig vector; Foundation Passport Prime screen-removal tamper; Coldcard clear case with exposed circuit for visual implant check.
risks: Destructive-open kills user-side 'open and compare' inspection (Ledger's 2018 stance) — pq1 must choose evidence-of-opening over inspectability deliberately and document it. Potting/welding complicates RMA and the SWD verification route (IMP-02). Does nothing against a factory-inserted implant that ships inside the sealed shell — that is IMP-02/IMP-03's job. Thermal/ESD rework of the display module needs ODM sign-off; EVT-003B-class units are already sealed and cannot be retrofitted.
